name: Ranggen
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village on the Innsbrucker Mittelgebirgsplateau, featuring traditional farmstead architecture and stunning views.
text:
Überblick

Ranggen is situated in the Innsbruck-Land district on a sun-drenched plateau of the Western Low Mountain Range, just west of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck at an elevation of 826 metres, home to around 1,140 inhabitants. The municipality nestles at the foot of the 1,939-metre-high Rangger Köpfl mountain, dropping steeply down toward the Inn Valley in the north. Its elevated terrace offers sweeping panoramic views across the peaks of the Nordkette, Mieming Range, and Wetterstein mountains. Ranggen preserves its traditional rural character with historic single-roof farmhouses and peaceful alpine meadows in close proximity to urban amenities.

Geschichte

The name Ranggen originates from the Middle High German term Rank, meaning slope curvature or terrace edge. A church was documented here as early as 1359. Historical importance was held by the Ferklehen estate, whose lords held the imperial ferry and river-crossing privilege across the unbridled Inn River to Zirl for centuries. An architectural jewel is the parish church of St. Magnus, constructed between 1775 and 1778 by master builder Franz Singer. The exquisite ceiling frescoes were painted by renowned artist Franz Anton Zeiller from Reutte, depicting Saint Magnus guarding the village and the Fourteen Holy Helpers. Its rococo sacristy is among the most ornate in Tyrol.

Anreise

Access to Ranggen is quick and convenient. By car, drivers leave the Inntalautobahn A12 at exit Zirl-Ost/Kematen or Zirl-West and follow the state road via Oberperfuss, reaching the mountain terrace in about 15 to 20 minutes from Innsbruck. Rail passengers take the S-Bahn Tirol to the Kematen in Tirol or Zirl stations down in the valley. From there, or directly from Innsbruck main railway station, VVT regional bus line 4166 provides scheduled service directly up to Ranggen.

Tipps

The local Rangger Köpfl mountain provides outstanding recreational activities year-round. Only 3 kilometres away in Oberperfuss, the modern Peter-Anich-Bahn gondola whisks visitors to Stiglreith, the Sulzstich reservoir lake, and the Rosskogelhütte refuge. Summer highlights include the Peter-Anich legends trail and demanding summit ascents up the 2,646-metre Rosskogel peak. During winter, the mountain features an approachable family ski area and a 10-kilometre natural toboggan track with regular floodlit night sledding. Directly from the village, hikers can explore the scenic Peter-Anich-Wanderweg trail connecting sunny plateau communities.
